exam_context: CLAT 2026 (UG) — Common Law Admission Test for admission to the 5-year integrated law programmes at 24 National Law Universities and several other participating institutions in India.
data_provenance: Estimated from the Consortium of NLUs' official CLAT 2026 exam pattern/syllabus notification (consortiumofnlus.ac.in) as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources (PhysicsWallah, Careers360, CollegeDekho, CollegeDunia, CLATapult, iQuanta), cross-checked Sep 2026. The per-section question COUNT is officially declared as a range (not a fixed number) and can vary within that band from year to year; treat the exact figures used here as the commonly-cited midpoint estimates for planning, not a guarantee of any single year's exact composition.

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple Sep 2026 sources describing the CLAT 2025/2026 marking pattern; unchanged since the 2024 format revision to 120 questions.
marking_scheme.sectional_cutoffs: None — CLAT does not impose sectional cut-offs; only the aggregate total score determines rank and seat allotment.
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct MCQ only, exclusively passage- or caselet-based across all five sections. No numerical-value, multiple-correct, or match-type questions.

exam_logistics.sectional_timing: None — candidates can allocate time across sections as they choose within the overall 120 minutes
exam_logistics.primary_language: English (may also be offered in select vernacular languages depending on the year's notification)

historical_format_note.pre_2020: 200 questions; Legal Aptitude section tested direct legal-principle knowledge; GK section tested static factual recall without passage dependency.
historical_format_note.2020_revamp: Question count reduced to 150; every section became passage-based; Legal Aptitude renamed Legal Reasoning; philosophy shifted from knowledge-testing to aptitude/comprehension-testing.
historical_format_note.2024_onward_current: Question count further reduced to 120 (from 150); this is the format still in effect for CLAT 2026.

indicative_cutoff_context.note: Rough, non-official score bands commonly cited by coaching trackers for reference only — actual cutoffs vary every year by category, university and reserved-seat quota.
